name: Gorgon CO2 Injection Project
source: IEEFA, Chevron, WA DMPE
notes: Injects into the Dupuy Formation saline aquifer and is underperforming. In FY2024-25 it captured 1.33 Mt, only about 25-30% of the CO2 removed from the gas stream, because of reservoir pressure constraints.
notes_research: Dupuy Fm saline aquifer; FY2024-25 captured 1.33 Mt, only ~25-30% of CO2 removed from gas stream due to reservoir pressure constraints. Underperforming.

name: Santos Moomba CCS
source: Santos, SPE JPT, CO2CRC
notes: Stores CO2 in depleted Cooper Basin gas reservoirs and passed 2 Mt in mid-2026. Phase 2 (with JX/ENEOS) targets 5 Mtpa by 2028, including third-party CO2 from Asia.
notes_research: Depleted Cooper Basin gas reservoirs; passed 2 Mt mid-2026; Phase 2 (JX/ENEOS) targets 5 Mtpa by 2028 incl. third-party Asian CO2.

name: CarbonNet Project (Pelican/Kookaburra)
source: djsir.vic.gov.au
notes: Two permitted offshore storage sites (Pelican and Kookaburra) with combined capacity of over 350 Mt. The project is in its Stage 3 development and commercial phase.
notes_research: Two permitted offshore sites, combined >350 Mt; Stage 3 Project Development & Commercial Establishment.

name: South West Hub (Collie CCS Hub)
source: WA CCUS Action Plan, zeroco2.no
notes: Targets the Triassic Lesueur Sandstone near Collie, Western Australia. Stalled for years, it was revived under the state's 2024 CCUS Action Plan and remains in appraisal.
notes_research: Triassic Lesueur Sandstone near Collie; stalled for years, revived under WA 2024 CCUS Action Plan. Appraisal/paused.

name: CO2CRC Otway Project
source: CO2CRC, CSLF
notes: A research facility for CO2 storage monitoring, with more than 13 years of monitoring research. Its Stage 3 work was recognized by the Carbon Sequestration Leadership Forum in 2025.
notes_research: Research/MMV facility; >13 years of monitoring research; Stage 3 recognized by CSLF 2025.

name: Bayu-Undan CCS
operator: Santos, SK E&S, INPEX, Eni, Tokyo Timor Sea Resources
source: Santos, Offshore Magazine, Tatoli
notes: Repurposes the depleted Bayu-Undan gas field, which ceased production in 2025. FEED is nearly complete, with FID targeted for 2025-26, injection from 2028 and capex of about US$1.6bn.
notes_research: Repurposing depleted Bayu-Undan gas field; production ceased 2025; FEED near-complete, FID target 2025-26, injection from 2028; ~US$1.6bn capex.

name: Tomakomai CCS Demonstration
source: JOGMEC, METI
notes: The demonstration injected about 300 kt of CO2 from 2016 to 2019. In FY2024 the area was re-selected as a JOGMEC Advanced CCS Project (JAPEX, Idemitsu, Hokkaido Electric) targeting about 1.5-2 Mtpa.
notes_research: Demo injected ~300 kt 2016-2019; area re-selected in FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS Projects (JAPEX/Idemitsu/Hokkaido Electric) targeting ~1.5-2 Mtpa.

name: Metropolitan Area (Kanto) Advanced CCS Project
operator: INPEX, Nippon Steel, Kanto Natural Gas Development
source: JOGMEC, Nippon Steel, Rigzone
notes: One of Japan's FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS Projects; in FY2025 its contract was extended for engineering and appraisal drilling.
notes_research: FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS Project; FY2025 contract extended for engineering/appraisal drilling.

name: Offshore Western Kyushu / Setouchi Advanced CCS Project
source: JOGMEC, MHI
notes: A FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS Project to store CO2 from refineries and thermal power plants in the Setouchi and Kyushu regions.
notes_research: FY2024 Advanced CCS Project; CO2 from Setouchi/Kyushu refineries and thermal plants.

name: Niigata Advanced CCS Project
source: JOGMEC FY2024
notes: One of nine FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS Projects; volumes are not yet public.
notes_research: Among 9 FY2024 Advanced CCS Projects; volumes not yet public.

name: Japan-Malaysia (Setouchi to Sarawak) Cross-border CCS
operator: JAPEX, Mitsubishi UBE Cement, Setouchi consortium
source: JAPEX, JOGMEC
notes: Would ship industrial CO2 from Japan's Setouchi region to offshore storage in Sarawak, Malaysia, at a target of 1.9-2.9 Mtpa. Listed as a FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS Project.
notes_research: Cross-border: Setouchi industrial CO2 shipped to offshore Sarawak; 1.9-2.9 Mtpa target; FY2024 JOGMEC Advanced CCS list.

name: CNOOC Enping 15-1 Offshore CCS
source: CNOOC, SCMP, China Daily
notes: An offshore CCS demonstration injecting into a saline formation about 800 m below the seabed, about 190 km southwest of Hong Kong. Over 100 million m3 had been injected by 2025; a Phase 2 expansion is under study.
notes_research: China's first offshore CCS demo; saline formation ~800m below seabed, ~190km SW of Hong Kong; >100M m3 injected by 2025; Phase 2 expansion under study.

name: China Energy (Guohua) Ordos CCUS Demonstration
source: Wang et al. 2021 (Greenhouse Gases Sci. Technol. 11:277); MIT CCS database
notes: A demonstration that injected about 300 kt of CO2 from a coal-to-liquids plant into deep saline formations at about 1,600 m. Injection ran from May 2011 to April 2015.
notes_research: Full-chain demo into deep saline formations; ~300 kt cumulative; distinct from Guohua Jinjie EOR (excluded). || 2026-10-15 verification: Shenhua/China Energy Ordos CTL plant, Ejin Horo Banner. ~300 kt injected May 2011 to April 2015 into low-permeability saline aquifers (~1,600 m, mostly Liujiagou Fm) per Wang et al. 2021; pilot scale 0.1 Mt/yr (MIT db). Unconfirmed 2019 news of resumed injection (Edinburgh SCCS db) not verified, so treated as concluded. Coordinates from Edinburgh SCCS db (secondary). Jinjie CCS is a separate, utilization/EOR project.

name: Huaneng Gansu Zhengning CCUS
source: GCCSI CCS Facility Profile, Sep 2026; SASAC Sept 2025
notes: Captures up to 1.5 Mtpa from a coal unit at Zhengning, sending about 1 Mtpa to enhanced oil recovery at the Changqing oil field and about 0.5 Mtpa to a nearby deep saline aquifer. Only the 0.5 Mtpa saline share is counted here as dedicated storage.
notes_research: World's largest coal-fired capture demo (1.5 Mtpa), operational Sept 2025; storage split geologic/EOR/green-fuel still emerging — verify dedicated-storage share. || 2026-10-15 verification: GCCSI profile (Sep 2026): 1.5 Mtpa capture (HNC-7 amine) on Zhengning Unit 1, operating since Sep 2025; ~1 Mtpa piped to Changqing oilfield for EOR, ~0.5 Mtpa via ~500 m pipeline to onshore deep saline aquifer ~3 km deep. Whether the saline injection is running at the full 0.5 Mtpa is not stated; cumulative stored unknown.

name: Sinopec Shengli Offshore CCS Phase 2 (Bohai)
source: Sinopec; ScienceDirect
notes: A Phase 2 concept to send post-combustion captured CO2 to offshore saline storage in the Bohai Sea, separate from the onshore Qilu-Shengli EOR project.
notes_research: Phase 2 concept: post-combustion capture to offshore saline storage; distinct from onshore Qilu-Shengli EOR (excluded).

name: China Resources Haifeng CCUS (Guangdong)
source: UK-China Guangdong CCUS Centre
notes: A long-stalled pre-feasibility project evaluating offshore saline storage in Guangdong.
notes_research: Long-stalled pre-feasibility; offshore saline storage under evaluation.

name: Korea Donghae-1 CCS
notes: A planned demonstration that would store CO2 from Ulsan-area industry in the depleted Donghae-1 gas field, which stopped producing in 2021. Its government feasibility review was reportedly withdrawn, with a re-application planned for 2026, so KNOC's 2030 start target is uncertain.
notes_research: Korea's first large-scale CCS; repurposed depleted Donghae-1 gas field (2004-2021); 1.2 Mtpa target 2025-2030, schedule slipping (still pre-FEED). || 2026-10-15 verification: KNOC 2025 ESG Highlights p.12: preliminary basic design for transport and storage complete; roadmap EPC 2027-28, operation 2030 (1.2 Mtpa). Yeta (preliminary feasibility) selected Jan 2024, KRW 2.95tn; withdrawal discussed Jul 2025 (Newsis); reported withdrawn, re-application targeted Q3 2026 (Asia Today, Mar 2026). No approval found as of Oct 2026.

name: Petronas Kasawari CCS
source: PETRONAS FID release (29 Nov 2022); PETRONAS Integrated Report 2022; MHB EPCIC release (29 Nov 2022); The Star (2 Apr 2026); Offshore Technology, Kasawari Gas Development Project
notes: Stores CO2 separated from Kasawari gas in the depleted M1 gas field, reached by a 138 km subsea pipeline. FID was taken in October 2022; the map location (Kasawari field, Central Luconia, about 200 km off Bintulu) is approximate.
notes_research: One of the largest offshore CCS projects regionally; gas production began Aug 2024; injection accelerated to 2027. || 2026-10-15 verification: FID approved 20 Oct 2022 (PETRONAS release 29 Nov 2022). Storage: neighbouring depleted field (PETRONAS IR 2022), M1 field via 138 km pipeline, 71-76 Mt total (MHB contractor release). Start-year history: end-2025 (MHB 2022), 2026 (PETRONAS IR 2022, 2024 feature), 2029-2030 (Borneo Post via GeoExpro), 2027 target (The Star 2 Apr 2026, secondary). Coordinates need checking: 3.6N/110.5E is west of Kuching, not 200 km off Bintulu.
source_research: NS Energy, The Star, Borneo Post

name: Petronas Lang Lebah CCS
source: Khor Reports
notes: Will store CO2 from the high-CO2, H2S-bearing Lang Lebah gas field. EPC bids came in over budget in early 2025, and the project is being re-engineered for a 2028 target.
notes_research: High CO2/H2S field; EPC bids over budget early 2025, in re-engineering; target 2028.

name: Petronas CCS Ventures Offshore Assessment
source: Petronas 2025
notes: Holds an offshore CO2 storage assessment permit, part of a strategy to make Malaysia an ASEAN storage hub. RINA won the FEED contract in October 2025.
notes_research: Malaysia's first offshore CO2 storage assessment permit; RINA FEED contract Oct 2025; ASEAN storage-hub strategy.

name: BP Tangguh UCC (Ubadari CCUS & Compression)
source: Hart Energy, BP
notes: Will store up to 15 Mt of CO2 over the field's life, with production starting around 2028. The $7bn project reached FID in November 2024.
notes_research: FID Nov 2024, $7bn; up to 15 Mt CO2 over field life; production start ~2028.

name: ExxonMobil/Pertamina Sunda-Asri CCS Hub
source: ICIS, Jakarta Globe
notes: A planned hub with up to 3 Gt of storage potential in the Sunda-Asri basins. ExxonMobil has committed up to $15bn including a petrochemical complex, and an amended agreement was signed in 2026.
notes_research: Up to 3 Gt potential in Sunda-Asri basins; ExxonMobil committed up to $15bn incl. petrochemical complex; A&R HoA signed 2026.

name: ONGC Gandhar CCS Pilot
source: Down to Earth 2025-26
notes: A planned ONGC pilot to inject about 100 t/day of captured CO2 into two depleted wells at the Gandhar oil field in Gujarat. It will also test CO2 for enhanced oil recovery, and the start of injection had not been confirmed by October 2026.
notes_research: India's first full-scale CCS pilot; ~100 t/day into two depleted wells at Gandhar oilfield; also tests EOR — verify dedicated-storage share. || 2026-10-15 verification: Jan 2026 reports (Outlook Business, Carbon Herald, Carbon Pulse): two abandoned onshore wells, ~100 t/d CO2 from Dahej-area industry and ONGC Hazira, into hydrocarbon reservoirs; also tests CO2-EOR. ONGC earlier injected CO2 from IOC Koyali refinery. No ONGC release or first-injection report found as of Oct 2026.

name: NTPC Pakri Barwadih CO2 Storage Appraisal
source: downtoearth.org.in 2025
notes: A dedicated CO2 storage appraisal borewell, drilled to about 1,200 m in late 2025; no injection yet.
notes_research: India's first dedicated geological CO2 storage appraisal borewell (~1,200m, late 2025); pre-injection.

name: PTTEP Arthit CCS
source: PTTEP press releases (8 Sep 2025; 9 Feb 2026)
notes: Stores CO2 separated from Arthit gas in reservoirs at 1,000-2,000 m depth, ramping up to about 1 Mtpa. PTTEP took FID in September 2025 and targets first storage in 2028.
notes_research: Thailand's first CCS; FID Sept 2025; depleted Arthit gas reservoirs 1,000-2,000m; ~$320M over 5 yr; Mitsui participating. || 2026-10-15 verification: FID 8 Sep 2025; up to ~1 Mtpa; storage start 2028; reservoirs 1,000-2,000 m; ~THB 10bn (USD 320M) over 5 yr (PTTEP 8 Sep 2025). Detailed engineering design phase as of PTTEP 9 Feb 2026. 'Mitsui participating' not found in PTTEP releases; removed. PTTEP says CO2 is injected 'back into its original subsurface reservoirs' (depleted_og kept).

name: CPC Tiezhenshan CCS Trial
source: SLB, Taipei Times
notes: An approved CCS trial (environmental assessment passed in 2023), injecting 300 kt over 3 years with monitoring in 2028-2030.
notes_research: Taiwan's first approved CCS (EIA passed 2023); 300 kt over 3 years, monitored 2028-2030.

name: Kapuni Gas Field CCS (prospective)
source: MBIE
notes: A candidate storage site, pending CCS legislation expected in 2026; no project is sanctioned yet.
notes_research: Prime NZ candidate pending CCS legislation (expected 2026); no sanctioned project yet.

name: Carbfix Hellisheiði (CarbFix1/CarbFix2 + Orca/Mammoth DAC injection)
source: Carbfix.com; Matter et al. 2016 Science; Wikipedia Carbfix
notes: A dedicated mineralization site injecting CO2 dissolved in water into basalt since 2012, with over 95% mineralized within about 2 years. It stores CO2 from the geothermal plant and from Climeworks' Orca and Mammoth DAC plants.
notes_research: World's first and longest-running dedicated ISM site. CarbFix1 pilot began 2012 (geothermal-plant CO2/H2S co-injected dissolved in water into basalt at ~400-800m, Hellisheiði geothermal plant); CarbFix2 scaled to capture ~12,000 t CO2/yr from the plant since 2014. Also hosts injection for Climeworks' Orca (4kt/yr, since 2021) and Mammoth (36kt/yr capacity, since 2024) DAC plants. >95% mineralization within ~2 years. Cumulative Carbfix-wide (geothermal + DAC) injected ~110,000+ t CO2 by 2025-26.

name: Carbfix Helguvík / CO2 Seastone (seawater dissolution pilot)
source: Carbfix.com 'Carbfix tests using seawater to mineralize CO2 at Helguvík'
notes: A pilot injecting CO2 dissolved in seawater, rather than freshwater, into basalt, about 400 m below sea level at Reykjanesbær. It uses CO2 imported from Switzerland to test the Coda Terminal import model.
notes_research: World's first injection of CO2 dissolved in seawater (rather than freshwater) into basaltic subsurface, ~400m depth below sea level, Reykjanesbær. Tests imported CO2 (from Switzerland) as a precursor/proof-of-concept for the Coda Terminal import model.

name: Carbfix Coda Terminal (Straumsvík CO2 import & storage hub)
source: Carbfix.com Coda Terminal page; EU Innovation Fund award; Carbfix 2026 guidance
notes: A hub to import captured CO2 by ship from Europe and mineralize it in basalt at Straumsvík. First imported injection is targeted for mid-2026 at about 500,000 t/yr, rising to 3 Mtpa by 2031.
notes_research: Large-scale hub to import captured CO2 by ship (from Europe, incl. Switzerland/Dan-Unity partners) and permanently mineralize it in basalt at Straumsvík near Reykjavik. First commercial imported-CO2 injection targeted mid-2026 (~500,000 t/yr with one ship); full capacity of 3 Mtpa (5 ships) targeted by 2031. On-site 'Silverstone' capture/receiving infrastructure under construction 2025-26.

name: Carbfix Nesjavellir Geothermal Reinjection
source: Carbfix.com operations overview
notes: Carbfix's second geothermal reinjection site, smaller than Hellisheiði and one of its four current injection sites in Iceland.
notes_research: Second Carbfix geothermal-plant reinjection site (Nesjavellir geothermal power station), smaller scale than Hellisheiði; part of Carbfix's four current Icelandic injection sites (Hellisheiði, Nesjavellir, Orca, Helguvík).

name: Reykjanes Ridge Sub-Seabed Basalt Pilot
operator: AIMS3 research consortium (MARUM, GEOMAR and partners)
source: Kopf et al. 2024, Carbon Capture Sci. Technol. 13, 100265, doi:10.1016/j.ccst.2024.100265
notes: A German-led research project (AIMS3) that has drilled monitoring boreholes on the Reykjanes Ridge flank, offshore southwest Iceland, to assess sub-seabed basalt storage. No CO2 has been injected; initial results were published in 2024.
notes_research: First sub-seabed basalt CO2 storage pilot on an active mid-ocean ridge segment offshore SW Iceland, extending the onshore Carbfix approach offshore; initial results reported 2024.
source_research: ScienceDirect 2024 'Initial results of a pilot project for sub-seabed basalt storage of carbon dioxide on the Reykjanes Ridge'

name: 44.01 Oman Original Pilot (Fizh/Samail massif)
source: JPT/SPE 2023 coverage; XPRIZE Carbon Removal 2023 winner profile
notes: 44.01's first demonstration injected CO2 dissolved in water into Samail ophiolite peridotite and showed mineralization in under 12 months. It earned a $1M XPRIZE Carbon Removal milestone award and led to Project Hajar.
notes_research: 44.01's original demonstration injecting CO2 dissolved in water into peridotite of the Samail ophiolite, proving <12-month mineralization; basis for the $1M XPRIZE Carbon Removal milestone award and subsequent Project Hajar scale-up.

name: 44.01 Project Hajar (Al Qabil, Hajar Mountains commercial-scale)
operator: 44.01 (with AirCapture DAC, Oman Ministry of Energy and Minerals)
source: 44.01.earth Project Hajar blog; Times of Oman; XPRIZE finalist profile
notes: A concession for commercial-scale peridotite mineralization, signed with Oman's Ministry of Energy and Minerals; the first borehole and injectivity tests were completed in 2023-24. Commercial buildout is still in development, and the map location is approximate.
notes_research: World's first concession for commercial-scale peridotite mineralization, signed with Oman's Ministry of Energy and Minerals at Al Qabil, Hajar Mountains. First borehole drilled and injectivity/safety tests completed 2023-24; co-located AirCapture modular DAC units (up to 500 t CO2/yr each). XFACTOR $1M award winner. Full commercial buildout still in development as of mid-2026; coordinates approximate (Hajar Mountains/Sharqiyah region).

name: 44.01 / ADNOC Fujairah Pilot
operator: 44.01 / ADNOC / Fujairah Natural Resources Corporation / Masdar
source: ADNOC press releases 2023, 2024; Carbon Herald; Gulf News Oct 2024
notes: Mineralized 10 tonnes of DAC-captured CO2, dissolved in seawater, in peridotite in under 100 days (2023-24).
notes_research: Pilot mineralized 10 tonnes of DAC-captured CO2 (dissolved in seawater) into peridotite in under 100 days (2023-24), UAE's first carbon-to-rock demonstration.

name: 44.01 / ADNOC Fujairah Scale-Up (Phase 1)
source: ADNOC press release Nov 2024 'ADNOC and 44.01 to Scale Up Carbon-to-Rock Project'; AGBI
notes: A scale-up phase, underway as of mid-2026, targeting over 300 tonnes of CO2 injected over a longer period. It contributes to ADNOC's 10 Mtpa carbon capture target for 2030.
notes_research: Scale-up phase targeting >300 tonnes CO2 injected over a longer duration, demonstrating pathway to larger deployment; part of ADNOC's 10 Mtpa 2030 carbon capture target. Status as of mid-2026: scale-up phase underway/ramping.

name: Octavia Carbon / Cella Project Hummingbird (Lake Elementaita, Kenya Rift)
source: decarbonfuse.com May 2026; Carbon Herald; XPRIZE Octavia & Cella profile
notes: A DAC plus mineral storage project near Lake Elementaita; an injection test announced in May 2026 put about 460 kg of CO2 into basalt using water-alternating-gas injection.
notes_research: First DAC+geologic mineral storage project in the Southern Hemisphere / Africa. First injection test May 2026: ~460 kg CO2 injected into basalt at ~9 kg/min using water-alternating-gas (WAG) technique adapted from EOR, near Lake Elementaita, Central Rift Valley. Targeting ~1,000 net tonnes removed/yr by end-2026 via 68 modular DAC units, powered by geothermal-adjacent grid.

name: Great Carbon Valley / Climeworks Kenya DAC+S (planned)
source: Climeworks press release; MIT Technology Review Dec 2025 'Welcome to Kenya's Great Carbon Valley'
notes: Great Carbon Valley and Climeworks are developing geothermal-powered DAC projects targeting up to 1 Mt CO2 per year stored by basalt mineralization in Kenya's Rift Valley. Site selection is at an early stage, and the map location is approximate.
notes_research: Nairobi-based systems integrator Great Carbon Valley partnering with Climeworks to develop DAC+S projects targeting up to 1 Mt CO2/yr removal via basalt mineralization in Kenya's Rift Valley, leveraging geothermal power (Olkaria/Menengai). Site selection and early development stage as of mid-2026; coordinates approximate (Rift Valley geothermal belt).

name: Ankeron Pacific Northwest DAC & Carbon Mineralization Hub
operator: RMI-led consortium (Carbfix, PNNL, Heirloom and others)
source: DOE FOA 2735 award; RMI press release; SSRN Ankeron Hub paper 2024
notes: A DOE-funded ($3M) feasibility study for a Pacific Northwest hub pairing DAC with mineral storage in Columbia River basalt. No permits or injection yet; the map location near Wallula is approximate.
notes_research: DOE-funded ($3M) feasibility/design study for a regional DAC + Columbia River Basalt mineral storage hub in eastern Washington/Pacific Northwest, combining multiple DAC technology developers with Carbfix/PNNL basalt-injection expertise. Feasibility study stage as of mid-2026; no injection yet. Coordinates approximate (Columbia River Basalt region near Wallula).
operator_research: RMI (lead), Carbfix, PNNL, Heirloom, Removr, Sustaera + 13-org consortium

name: Deep Sky / Carbfix Thetford Mines Pilot Injection
source: Newswire 'Deep Sky completes Quebec's first geological injection of captured carbon'; Deep Sky blog
notes: A geological CO2 injection pilot using the Carbfix mineralization method in serpentinite of the historic Thetford Mines asbestos belt. A companion pre-feasibility study is underway at the Bécancour industrial park for a larger storage site.
notes_research: Quebec's first geological CO2 injection using the Carbfix mineralization method, at the historic Thetford Mines asbestos/serpentinite belt. First North American mineralization injection by Deep Sky. Companion pre-feasibility study underway at Bécancour industrial park (SPIPB) for a larger sedimentary/mineral storage site.

name: CO2 Lock SAM Project (Brucite-Serpentinite, Central BC)
source: CO2 Lock news release 25 Jan 2024 (newsfilecorp.com/release/195720); FPX Nickel release
notes: A CO2 injection test in brucite-rich serpentinized peridotite at CO2 Lock's SAM site, about 50 km southwest of Prince George in central British Columbia. The company reported a successful injection in January 2024.
notes_research: First-ever successful CO2 injection into brucite-rich ultramafic (serpentinized peridotite) rock, at the SAM property in central British Columbia, near FPX Nickel's Decar Ni project. Builds on ~decade of Decar tailings mineralogy research. Field program completed; further site characterization ongoing across BC ultramafic belts (Decar, Cassiar, Shulaps, Atlin).
source_research: FPX Nickel/CO2 Lock press release Jan 2024; Mining Stock Education

name: PNNL Wallula Basalt Pilot
operator: PNNL / Big Sky Carbon Sequestration Partnership (Boise White Paper Mill site)
source: PNNL Wallula Basalt Project page; McGrail et al. 2017 Environ. Sci. Technol.; ResearchGate 'Quantification of CO2 Mineralization at the Wallula Basalt Pilot Project'
notes: Injected about 977 t of CO2 in 2013 into Columbia River basalt near Wallula, Washington. Coring found up to 60% of the injected carbon mineralized as ankerite within about 2 years, demonstrating basalt mineralization at pilot scale.
notes_research: DOE Regional Carbon Sequestration Partnership Phase II pilot; ~977 t (~1 kt) CO2 injected in 2013 into Columbia River Basalt Group interflow zones near Wallula, WA. Post-injection coring (2015-2016) found up to 60% of injected carbon mineralized as ankerite within ~2 years, demonstrating basalt ISM feasibility at pilot scale. Concluded; foundational for later Ankeron Hub and Cascadia CarbonSAFE offshore studies.

name: Sleipner CO2 Storage
source: Global CCS Institute; Equinor; IEEFA 2023
notes: Industrial-scale dedicated CO2 storage, injecting into the Utsira Sand saline aquifer at about 800-1000 m depth.
notes_research: Utsira Sand saline aquifer, ~800-1000m depth. First industrial-scale dedicated CO2 storage project globally. >26 Mt cumulative by 2026 at ~1.0 Mtpa.

name: Snøhvit CO2 Storage
source: Global CCS Institute; Equinor
notes: Stores CO2 separated at the Snøhvit LNG plant in Barents Sea saline aquifers. Injection moved from the Tubåen to the Stø Formation in 2011 after pressure problems.
notes_research: CO2 from Snøhvit LNG plant injected into Tubåen/Stø Fm saline aquifer, Barents Sea. Storage zone changed from Tubåen to Stø Fm in 2011 after pressure issues.

name: Northern Lights CCS Phase 1
source: Equinor Aug 2025 'First CO2 volumes stored at Northern Lights'; norlights.com
notes: Began receiving CO2 from Heidelberg Materials' Brevik cement plant in August 2025, injecting about 2,600 m below the seabed into the Johansen Formation.
notes_research: First CO2 receipt/injection from Heidelberg Materials Brevik cement plant began Aug 2025, ~2,600m below seabed, Johansen Fm, North Sea. Phase 1 capacity 1.5 Mtpa.

name: Northern Lights CCS Phase 2 Expansion
source: Equinor Mar 2025 press release; JPT Apr 2025
notes: A NOK 7.5bn expansion approved in March 2025 that adds about 3.5 Mtpa, raising total injection capacity from 1.5 to at least 5 Mtpa. It is expected to be ready in the second half of 2028, with Stockholm Exergi as a new customer.
notes_research: NOK 7.5bn investment approved Mar 2025 to expand total injection capacity from 1.5 to at least 5 Mtpa; new customer Stockholm Exergi; expected ready H2 2028.

name: Quest CCS (Shell Scotford, Alberta)
source: Shell; Global CCS Institute
notes: Captures CO2 from hydrogen production at the Scotford Upgrader and injects it through 3 wells into the Basal Cambrian Sands saline aquifer, about 2 km deep.
notes_research: Captures CO2 from Scotford Upgrader hydrogen production, injects into Basal Cambrian Sands saline aquifer ~2km depth near Thornhill, AB via 3 wells. >11 Mt cumulative by 2026.

name: Illinois Industrial CCS (ADM Decatur)
source: EPA enforcement order 2024-25; E&E News 'Carbon storage site that leaked set to restart injections'; sequestration.mit.edu
notes: A commercial-scale saline storage project under an EPA Class VI permit (2017), injecting corn-processing CO2 into the Mount Simon Sandstone. EPA issued a compliance order in 2024-25 after injected fluid migrated into an unauthorized zone, with no public health impact.
notes_research: First commercial-scale saline storage project in the US operating under EPA Class VI permit (effective 2017), injecting CO2 from corn-processing/ethanol into Mt. Simon Sandstone. EPA issued a compliance order in 2024-25 after injected fluid migrated into an unauthorized zone ~5,000 ft below surface (no public health impact); ADM undertaking corrective monitoring, restarting/continuing injections under order as of mid-2026.

name: Broadwing Energy Center CCS (Decatur, IL)
source: IL EPA draft air permit Apr 2026; Global Energy Monitor; Modern Power Systems
notes: A 452 MW gas-fired cogeneration plant supplying ADM and Google, designed to capture about 90% of its CO2 for injection into ADM's existing Class VI wells. FID was targeted for Q2 2026 and commercial operation for 2030.
notes_research: 452 MW gas-fired cogeneration plant in Decatur, IL supplying ADM and Google; ~90% of CO2 emissions to be captured and injected into ADM's existing EPA Class VI wells (Mt. Simon Sandstone). Draft air construction permit issued Apr 2026 (comment period to Jun 2026); FID targeted Q2 2026; commercial operation targeted 2030.

name: In Salah CCS (Algeria)
source: IEAGHG; Global CCS Institute
notes: Injected about 3.8 Mt of CO2 stripped from natural gas into the Krechba Formation from 2004 to 2011. Injection was suspended over caprock integrity and microseismicity concerns, and the site is now a long-running monitoring case study.
notes_research: CO2 stripped from produced natural gas injected into Krechba Fm saline sandstone flanking gas field 2004-2011 (~3.8 Mt total); injection suspended in 2011 over caprock integrity/microseismicity concerns; project concluded, long-running monitoring case study.

name: ADNOC Habshan CCUS (Bab Far North Field)
source: ADNOC FID release; Petrofac $615M contract award; Drilling Contractor
notes: Will capture 1.5 Mtpa and permanently store it in the Bab Far North Field (dedicated storage, not EOR), raising ADNOC's capture capacity to 2.3 Mtpa. Commissioning is targeted for 2026.
notes_research: ADNOC FID'd 1.5 Mtpa CCUS facility at Habshan, Al Gharbia; CO2 to be injected and permanently stored (dedicated geological storage, not EOR) in the Bab Far North Field. Would triple ADNOC's capture capacity to 2.3 Mtpa. Commissioning targeted 2026; largest CCUS project in MENA at FID.

name: Porthos CCS (Netherlands)

notes_research: Greece's first CCS project and an EU Project of Common Interest (PCI). Depleted Prinos and Epsilon oil fields, Gulf of Kavala, N. Aegean Sea (~8km NW of Thassos island, ~18km S of Kavala mainland, water depth ~30-50m); CO2 to be injected at 2,700-3,000m below seabed into a saline sand unit beneath the depleted oil reservoir — dedicated storage, not EOR. 25-year CO2 storage permit granted to EnEarth by HEREMA (Greek hydrocarbon regulator), confirmed Feb 26 2026. Phase 1 capacity ~1 Mtpa (2025-2028), rising to up to ~2.8-3 Mtpa by 2029 as further CO2 sources (incl. imported) are connected.

Operational since August 2025 at ~3,000 t CO2/yr; distinct from Deep Sky's separate Thetford Mines, Quebec mineralization pilot (serpentinite, already tracked) and its Bécancour pre-feasibility study — Alpha is geologic saline storage, not in-situ mineralization.

notes_research: Brazil's first dedicated (non-EOR, non-pre-salt) saline-aquifer CO2 storage pilot, distinct from Petrobras' large-volume Santos Basin pre-salt CO2-EOR reinjection program (excluded from this inventory as EOR). CO2 captured at the Cabiúnas natural-gas treatment unit (Macaé) piped ~78km to a compression station at Barra do Furado, Quissamã, Rio de Janeiro state, for injection into an onshore deep saline reservoir. Approved by Petrobras board Sept 2025 (regulated by ANP/INEA); ~100,000 t/yr (0.1 Mtpa) over an initial 3-year pilot; construction/engineering underway toward a targeted ~2028 start.

name: KAUST/Aramco Jizan Basalt Mineralization Pilot

notes_research: First basalt in-situ mineralization field pilot in the Arabian Peninsula, methodologically similar to Carbfix (CO2-charged water re-injected through two wells, several hundred meters deep, with groundwater recirculation), in the basalt of the Jizan Economic Complex/Red Sea coastal plain, SW Saudi Arabia. ~131 t CO2 injected over a ~10-month pilot (2024-25); ~70% trapped as solid carbonate minerals within the study period; results published in Nature Apr 2026. Regional basalt formation claimed to hold multi-Gt theoretical capacity, but no commercial scale-up site yet announced as of mid-2026 — pilot concluded, coordinates approximate (Jizan region).

No capacity or scale-up figures published as of mid-2026.

notes: Would capture CO2 at Heidelberg Materials' Devnya cement plant and store it in the depleted Galata gas field offshore in the Black Sea. A pilot capture unit has run since October 2023; full-chain operation is targeted for 2028 at the earliest.

notes_research: Depleted Camelot gas field plus associated saline aquifers, southern North Sea (storage license CS019); total storage potential estimated 70-100 Mt, target injection rate up to 6.5 Mtpa.
